cells.remarks: Describes the division of Alande-1000 and the place Kampanavāda and their ruler Dāmka, son of Āhavamalla States that when mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Dhanasaṁgraharaśa, the Śilāhāra chief of Tarddavāḍi, was governing the fort of Attinūru, he, along with the prabhu-gāmuṇḍgaḷu of Attinūru-80 and heggaḍe Bamayya, endowed 20 mattar of land situated in the field of Arasimge to āryya Śivadēvayya for the purpose of worship and offerings to the god Mallikārjunadēva at Chillamela on the bank of the Bhimarathi river Also records further grants of land in Arasimge and Kēkarasā-ṇige-sime to the gods Sātēśvara and Mallikārjunadēva by Prabhu Dāmka-gāvuṇḍa and his son Gōna-gauḍa In characters of about the 12th century

cells.location: GOBBŪR
cells.place: Slab fixed into the inner wall at the right side in the Īśvara temple
cells.date: Regnal year 2, Vibhava, Puṣya, Amāvāse, Monday Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti, Solar eclipse Irregular
cells.remarks: Pura, accompanied by his rāṇivāsa and officers, Srikaraṇas and pradhānas, after bathing in the sacred river Bhīmarathu at Chullameḷa, made a series of gifts to the god Śrīsaila Mallikārjuna on the occasion of arddhōdaya-sūryagrahaṇa The grant is said to have been made following the renovation of the temple, in an assembly of prabhugaṇḍu, seṭṭumukha, nakharā, mummuri-daṇḍa of Liṅgāpura and Attunūru-80, mahā-maṇḍalēśvara-manneya Boppadēva, Liṅgārasa, Dākarasa, the 18 santatis, the se[ṭṭi]s guttas of Alande-1000 and others. Damaged Records the grant of lands, oil mill, etc by the administrator (manneya-prabhu) along with the mūliga, hiṭṭu, sama-sta-praje and nakara of Santeya Gobbūru, situated in Alande-nāḍu, for worship and offerings to the god Kaḷhēdēva Mentions Kalyāṇaśakti, the āchārya of the temple In characters of the 12th century

cells.date: Śaka 1205, (current) Śrāvaṇa śu 10, Thursday = 1282 A D, July 16
cells.remarks: Commences with the praise of the Jaina teachers Records the gift of land for the services of amṛtapadi of the deity Ādidēva (i e, Ādinātha) of the Nakharā-jmālaya, by Bālachandra, the disciple of Nēmachandra-paṇḍita of the Nāgalēśvara-dēśiya-gaṇa of Mūla samgha, referred to as mahāmaṇḍalā-chārya and rājaguru and by the samasta-māṇkyanagaras of the Belugula-tīrtha, the lay disciples of Māghanandisiddhānta-chakravarti, who was also mentioned as the rājaguru of the Hoysala kings It also records a number of wet-lands and money for various services such as amṛtapadi, vaḍḍarangapūje during dīpāvali, abhishēka-pūje, aṣṭhavidharchchane, puṣpāñjali and for the purpose of saṅkramaṇa, Jīvadayā-ṣṭami, perpetual lamp, khaṇḍasphuṭajir-nōddhāra etc by various other persons of the place Published in Ep Carn (Rev), Vol II, Ins No 456

cells.location: ANDĀRU
cells.place: Slab lyng on the edge of a field
cells.remarks: Damaged Records that the chief made on the day of Solar eclipse provisions for the worship, offerings and services of the god Viṣṇudēva at Hosakalambatha by granting paddy measuring mudis from the yield of a newly levelled land of 12 beṭṭu situated at Alaṁtueya-Kajane The land was stated to have been obtained by Sukrapasēnabōva and Kukelmga-sēnabōva, sons of Pamdaṁ-sēnabōva of Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Ṛik-śākhā, from Gōpaṇa-adhikāri of Alaṁtueya-ma[ṇḍru] after converting it into permanent holding (mūla)
